sections.html:
The Department of English Philology was created in 1990 on the basis of the Department of Roman and Germanic Philology, which had existed since 1986. In October 2022, the Department was expanded as it was joined by the English Language Department.

The Department of English Philology was headed by Professor Nataliia Tuchyna, PhD (Education), from 1986 to 2000, and by Associate Professor Ihor Kamynin, PhD (Philology), from 2000 to 2021. Since April 2021, Nataliia Tuchyna has resumed the position of the Head of the Department.

The teaching staff comprises 19 teachers, 2 professors and 16 Associate Professors among them. 2 more Professors are working as part-time teachers (L. Kornilieva and O. Kovalenko). All teachers have been upgrading their skills at different leading universities in Ukraine and abroad, have participated in numerous scientific conferences and webinars as well as several international projects. Nowadays, the following teachers have been the members of the Department: Professor Lilia Kornilieva, Doctor of Sciences (Philology); Professor Yana Levchenko, Doctor of Sciences (Education); Professor O. Kovalenko, Doctor of Sciences (Education); Professor Tamila Shcheblykina, Doctor of Sciences (Education); Associate Professor Hanna Krapivnyk, Doctor of Sciences (Philosophy); Professor Nataliia Tuchyna, PhD (Education); Associate Professor Nina Alekseyeva, PhD (Philology); Associate Professor Oksana Bezkorovaina, PhD (Philology), Associate Professor Maryna Bielova, PhD (Philology); Lecturer Maryna Vassylieva, PhD (Education); Associate Professor Yulia Hetman, PhD (Philology); Associate Professor Inna Zharkovska, PhD (Philology); Senior Lecturer Raisa Istomina; Associate Professor Zhanna Kononova, PhD (Philology); Associate Professor Lada Krasovitska, PhD (Philology); Associate Professor Tetyana Petrenko, PhD (Education); Associate Professor Tetyana Razumenko, PhD (Education); Associate Professor Tetyana Starostenko, PhD (Philology); Associate Professor Olha Ukrainska, PhD (Education); Associate Professor Yulia Shchpak, PhD (Philology); Associate Professor Olena Kholodnyak, PhD (Philology).
